draft.title: Codominance and incomplete dominance
card: In some genes, neither allele hides the other. A heterozygous organism (one with two different alleles) then shows a phenotype that is not simply one parent's trait.
both alleles show fully and separately in the heterozygote. In human ABO blood, a person with alleles IA and IB has type AB blood, with both A and B markers on the red blood cells.
neither allele is fully expressed, so the heterozygote has a blend between the two parent traits. Red-flowered and white-flowered snapdragon plants can give pink-flowered offspring.
In incomplete dominance, a cross of two pink plants gives red, pink and white offspring in a 1:2:1 ratio. The heterozygote looks different from both homozygotes.
draft.remember: Codominance shows both traits side by side. Incomplete dominance shows a blend in between.

a.q: A person has the genotype IA IB and their red blood cells carry both A markers and B markers. Which pattern of inheritance does this show?
opts: Codominance, as both alleles show fully
Incomplete dominance, as the alleles blend
Complete dominance, as one allele hides the other
Recessive inheritance, as two copies are needed
a.why: Both alleles are expressed fully and separately, so this is codominance. It is not incomplete dominance, because the two markers are not mixed into one in-between trait.
a.clue: Look at whether both markers appear in full or a mix forms.

b.q: A grower crosses two pink-flowered snapdragon plants. Pink is the heterozygote of a red allele and a white allele, and neither allele is dominant. What offspring are expected?
b.why: Each pink parent passes on a red or a white allele with equal chance. The offspring are 1 red, 2 pink and 1 white, as the heterozygote looks different from both homozygotes. A 3:1 ratio would need one allele to be dominant.
b.clue: Heterozygotes look different here, so count them as their own group.

a.best: Codominance, as both alleles show fully
